newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek navy aid ship docks at rebel-held Sarande.
newsitem.headline: Greek navy aid ship docks at rebel-held Sarande.

text.p: A Greek navy minesweeper docked at Albania's rebel-held southern port of Sarande on Thursday under heavy guard to protect its cargo of humanitarian aid from potential looters, witnesses said.
Hundreds of people crowded around the picturesque port when the Atalante arrived with food and medicine. The town's rebel council dispatched a heavy guard to make sure none of the goods were stolen.

Many shops and buildings in Sarande have been looted in recent days and armed gangs, heavily armed with weapons stolen from state arsenals, have begun robbing motorists and travellers at the Greek border.
The Greek consul from nearby Gjirokaster, Nikos Kanellos, showed up with seven bodyguards who pushed their way through the crowd to oversee the unloading of the cargo.

Three trucks with armed guards sped medicine, milk, wheat, and other supplies 100 metres (yards) to a warehouse which had gunmen posted outside. The rebel council has appointed a special committee to oversee the distribution of the aid.
